record.field: Load the instructions and tools of one or more skills by id, making them available for the rest of this conversation. Skills are only loaded progressively, on demand: only the tools of a skill you have actually loaded are usable, so call this before using any tool that belongs to a skill you have not loaded yet.

Ask the user a short clarifying question when a request is ambiguous or a choice must be made before you can continue. Offer 2 to 4 concrete options; ask only one question at a time and wait for the answer before doing anything else.

List the Odoo models this assistant is allowed to query, with their label and, when it has one, the main menu path a human would use to find it. Call this first when you are not sure which model holds the data the user is asking about; it takes no arguments. Once you have a model name, call get_fields before searching it so you use real field names instead of guessing them.

List the fields of a model: technical name, label, type (with the related model in parentheses for relational fields), flags (req = required, ro = read-only, search = searchable, sort = sortable) and, for selection fields, the allowed key=label pairs. Always call this before search/read_records/read_group on a model you have not inspected yet in this conversation, so you use the exact field names the model actually has.

{"type": "object", "properties": {"model_name": {"type": "string", "description": "Technical model name, e.g. res.partner"}, "include_description": {"type": "boolean", "description": "Also include each field's help text"}}, "required": ["model_name"]}

Search a model and return a page of matching records. The domain is a standard Odoo domain, given as a Python/JSON list of ["field", "operator", value] triples, e.g. [["state", "=", "done"], ["amount_total", ">", 100]]; combine conditions with the prefix operators "&" (and, the default between consecutive conditions), "|" (or) and "!" (not), e.g. ["|", ["city", "=", "Rotterdam"], ["city", "=", "Amsterdam"]]. Supported operators include =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, not in, like, ilike and child_of. For relative dates (e.g. "created last week"), call compute_date first and use its value in the domain rather than guessing a date. Results are paginated (limit is clamped between 1 and 200, default 50); check has_more and increase offset to get the next page. Omit fields to get a sensible default set, or pass an explicit list from get_fields.

{"type": "object", "properties": {"model_name": {"type": "string"}, "domain": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string", "description": "Odoo domain as a Python/JSON list literal, e.g. \"[['state', '=', 'done']]\"; an empty list matches everything"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type":["string","integer","number","boolean","array"],"items":{"type":["string","integer","number","boolean","array"],"items":{"type":["string","integer","number","boolean"]}}}}]}, "fields": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Field names to return; omit for a sensible default set"}, "offset": {"type": "integer"}, "limit": {"type": "integer"}, "order": {"type": "string", "description": "e.g. 'create_date desc' or 'name asc, id desc'"}}, "required": ["model_name"]}

Read a specific, already-known list of record ids on a model (up to 50 at a time). Never guess ids: get them from a previous search or from the record the user is currently looking at. Ids that no longer exist, or that you are not allowed to read, are reported in missing_ids instead of causing an error. Set include_files to true (for 5 or fewer records) to also receive their linked images/PDF attachments as inline content.

{"type": "object", "properties": {"model_name": {"type": "string"}, "record_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer"}}, "fields": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}, "include_files": {"type": "boolean", "description": "Also return linked image/PDF attachments as inline content (5 records max)"}}, "required": ["model_name", "record_ids"]}

Group and aggregate records, e.g. "count of orders per country" or "total amount per month". groupby items are a field name, or "field:granularity" for date/datetime fields (granularity one of year, quarter, month, week, day). aggregates items are "field:function" (function one of sum, avg, min, max, count, count_distinct) or the special "__count" for a plain row count. Use compute_date beforehand for any relative date boundaries in the domain. Prefer this over search when the user wants totals, counts or breakdowns rather than a list of individual records.

{"type": "object", "properties": {"model_name": {"type": "string"}, "domain": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string", "description": "Odoo domain as a Python/JSON list literal"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": ["string", "integer", "number", "boolean", "array"], "items": {"type": ["string", "integer", "number", "boolean", "array"], "items": {"type": ["string", "integer", "number", "boolean"]}}}}]}, "groupby": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "e.g. [\"country_id\", \"create_date:month\"]"}, "aggregates": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "e.g. [\"amount_total:sum\", \"__count\"]"}, "having": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string", "description": "Domain over the aggregate names, e.g. \"[['__count', '>', 5]]\""}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": ["string", "integer", "number", "boolean", "array"], "items": {"type": ["string", "integer", "number", "boolean", "array"], "items": {"type": ["string", "integer", "number", "boolean"]}}}}]}, "offset": {"type": "integer"}, "limit": {"type": "integer"}, "order": {"type": "string", "description": "One of the groupby or aggregate items exactly as given, plus asc or desc, e.g. 'amount_total:sum desc' or '__count desc'"}}, "required": ["model_name"]}

Turn a relative date expression ("yesterday", "last month", "next Friday at 5pm", "the first Monday of last month") into the exact string to use for field_name in a domain, computed in the user's own timezone. Always use this instead of computing or guessing dates yourself; the model does not reliably know today's date, the user's timezone, or how many days are in a given month. operations are applied in order: {"type": "navigate", "period": "day|week|month|quarter|year|hour|minute", "offset": -1, "boundary": "start|end|none"} shifts by whole periods and optionally snaps to the start/end of the resulting period (weeks start on Monday); {"type": "find_previous"|"find_next", "weekday": 0-6 (Monday=0)} jumps to the nearest such weekday, not counting today. An optional pin then fixes the day of month (an integer, or {"weekday": 0-6, "occurrence": 1-5 or -1 for "last"}) and/or the time of day ("HH:MM" or "HH:MM:SS"). The returned value is 'YYYY-MM-DD' for a Date field or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' in UTC for a Datetime field.

Create one or more new records on a model. Always call get_fields on the model first so you use its real field names, types and required fields; never guess a field name or invent an id. Write a short, plain-language explanation of what you are about to create and why, so the user can review it before anything happens. "values" is a list of records to create (max 20); each record's "field_values" is a list of {"field": technical field name, "value": the value to set, "x2m_link_ids": an id or list of ids} entries. Use "value" for every field except many2many/one2many ones: for a many2one, "value" is the target record's id (search for it first, e.g. with search or read_records, rather than guessing it); for many2many/one2many fields leave "value" empty and put the ids of the existing records to link in "x2m_link_ids" instead (this tool can only link existing records, it cannot create related records in the same call). This tool always shows the user a preview of exactly what will be created first and only writes to the database once they confirm; do not tell the user something was created until you see the confirmed result.

{"type": "object", "properties": {"explanation": {"type": "string", "description": "Plain-language explanation of what you are about to create and why, shown to the user"}, "model_name": {"type": "string"}, "values": {"type": "array", "maxItems": 20, "description": "Records to create", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {"field_values": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {"field": {"type": "string", "description": "Technical field name"}, "value": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "number"}, {"type": "boolean"}, {"type": "null"}]}, "x2m_link_ids": {"anyOf": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer"}}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "For many2many/one2many fields only: id(s) of existing records to link"}}, "required": ["field"]}}}, "required": ["field_values"]}}, "preview_menu_id": {"anyOf": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Optional id of a menu whose action opens this model, used to build a nicer link to the created record(s)"}}, "required": ["explanation", "model_name", "values"]}

Change the values of records that already exist. Always call get_fields first, and search beforehand for the exact records you mean to change, so the domain you pass here targets only those; a domain that would match every record on the model (an empty domain, or an always-true condition such as an id filter every record satisfies) is refused, on purpose. "updates" is a list of {"model_name", "domain", "changes"} groups (max 50; usually you only need one), each matching at most 200 records; each "changes" item is {"field": technical field name, "value": the new value, "x2m_commands": null or a JSON string for many2many/one2many fields only}. Use "value" for every field except many2many/one2many ones, where "x2m_commands" must instead be a JSON string such as {"link": [ids to add]}, {"unlink": [ids to remove]}, {"set": [ids that should be the only ones linked]} or {"clear": true} (only existing records can be linked; never invent an id). Write a short, plain-language explanation of the change, and when a field being changed represents a status or stage, also explain what changing it will do. This tool always shows the user a preview of the old and new value of every affected record first and only writes to the database once they confirm; do not tell the user something was updated until you see the confirmed result.
